analysis.title: Are AAs The New Junk? Goldman Says Move Down In Quality Because The Highest-Rated Borrowers Are Drowning In AI Debt (2027 Global Credit Outlook: Fading Tailwinds and a Growing AI Divide)
key_insights: Goldman forecasts a -0.5% excess return for USD investment grade in 2027 against a post-GFC median of +2.0%, after about 0.5% in 2026. USD high yield is forecast at +0.3% against a 5.6% median.

Spread forecasts: USD IG widens from 91bps to 105bps by end-2027, USD HY from 337bps to 410bps. Goldman expects some technical tightening into year-end 2026 as supply wanes. EUR IG widens more front-loaded, to 110bps in Q1 2027 (election calendar, energy risk, France), then drifts back.
The article's duration math: with USD IG duration of 6.6, 14bps of widening takes roughly 0.9% off prices, about the full spread carry earned over a year, which produces the negative excess return.
Goldman says a more resilient growth picture is unlikely to push spreads much tighter, because periods of macro stability are met by outsized issuance that competes for capital.

Starting valuations are tight at the top and wide at the bottom: USD IG spreads at the 14th percentile of their range since 2010 (about the 2nd at the start of 2026), USD BBB at the 16th, USD HY at the 23rd, CCC at the 93rd percentile in dollars and 99th in euros.
Goldman forecasts record USD IG gross supply of $2.4 trillion and net supply of $1.15 trillion in 2027. Drivers are AI financing, maturity walls, strategic M&A and US issuers borrowing in euros.
Hyperscalers collectively reported negative free cash flow in 3Q2026. Goldman says debt market access is now a strategic competitive advantage in the AI buildout.

AI-related gross issuance is nearly $700 billion globally so far in 2026, of which $296 billion came from the five hyperscalers (Goldman's 2026 hyperscaler forecast was $250 billion). For 2027 Goldman expects $440 billion of direct hyperscaler issuance (assuming 35% of capex is debt-financed), versus $108 billion in 2025, plus $545 billion of AI project finance. The article's author calls $440 billion a floor.

Of the 27 USD IG deals of $10 billion or more in 2026, 66% were AI-related. New issue concessions on AI paper were roughly 18bps in November against under 7bps for other issuers (approximate, read off a chart). Goldman says 'more than price will be needed in 2027', namely clearer monetization and funding plans.

Goldman advises moving down in quality within IG, favoring BBBs over AAA, AA and A. AAA/AA issuers generated 22% of USD IG supply and 15% of EUR IG supply in 2026, the highest shares since 2016 and 2018, and AI issuance is concentrated among higher-rated issuers. USD AA spreads moved from about the 9th percentile in January to the 50th, the cheapest of any IG rating bucket in dollars.
In high yield, BBs have been a record 67% of USD HY supply in 2026 and AI project finance is expected to add to it, so Goldman prefers single-Bs over BBs.

Goldman now prefers USD IG over HY, dropping the neutral stance held since August, with low conviction because the HY/IG spread ratio is at the 83rd percentile. The article says Morgan Stanley made the same call earlier in the week.

Goldman says recent flattening of AI-related back-end curves, as hyperscalers shifted to shorter-dated debt, reflects too much comfort with smaller pull-forward issuance. It expects longer-term contingent guarantees to put a floor under long-end spreads. The article cites a $2.8 trillion estimate of off-balance-sheet leases and backstops across five hyperscalers (Lynam, last month).

Sector positioning: underweight Technology in IG and moving underweight USD HY Technology. Overweights remain Banks, Energy and Health Care. Less negative on airlines, paper and packaging and parts of consumer discretionary. Cutting rate-sensitive REITs and autos.

Other calls: prefers non-financial hybrids to BB high yield and sees compelling value in money center banks' tier 2 sub debt. HY bonds are preferred to leveraged loans in both regions on carry, quality and loan refinancing risk tied to software exposure. Goldman stays cautious on AT1s through Q1 because of potential sovereign risk spillovers into financials ahead of the April and May French presidential elections.

Default forecasts for 2027: 4% USD HY, 5% USD leveraged loans, 5% EUR HY, 4% EUR loans, the latter three above long-run averages. Average interest coverage for USD CCC issuers is below 1.0x. Recoveries on senior unsecured USD HY bonds are around $30, down from about $40 in 2021.

Private credit: per PitchBook LCD, 32% of US private equity inventories are aged six years or more, the highest share since data began in 2000. Goldman's private credit growth areas for 2027 are AI funding and lending to software companies facing a maturity wall. Dry powder in the higher-octane strategies is above $245 billion.

Goldman recommends keeping macro hedges in portfolios in 2027, because AI risks (capacity constraints or insufficient monetization) are more likely to spill into broader macro weakness. It suggests using strength, especially into year-end, to reset hedges. Implied vol on the main credit indices is well below its 2022 peak, so protection is reasonably priced.

Goldman's base case is wider spreads, with most markets landing between the 30th and 50th percentile of post-GFC outcomes, which it frames as greater issuer-level dispersion rather than broad market disruption.

risk_factors: Delayed monetization, rising purchase commitments and further capex increases could push hyperscaler issuance above Goldman's forecast (Goldman's own listed upside risks to supply).
AI risks, namely capacity constraints or insufficient monetization, could spill into broader macro weakness in 2027.
Investors have cleared AI supply on price alone, and Goldman says more than price will be needed in 2027, namely monetization clarity and funding plans.
Contingent guarantees, including leases and backstops estimated at $2.8 trillion across five hyperscalers, sit off balance sheet.
CCC issuers have average interest coverage below 1.0x, and senior unsecured USD HY recoveries have fallen to about $30.
Private equity inventory aging (32% held six years or more) with more leverage on older vintages, and private credit dependent on deal flow that has not arrived.
French sovereign risk spilling into European financials, with French borrowing costs at a two-decade high.

tension_points.theme: AI debt supply and credit spreads
tension_points.bull_case: Goldman's base case is wider spreads that land most markets between the 30th and 50th percentile of post-GFC outcomes, which it calls greater issuer-level dispersion rather than broad market disruption. Price has cleared the market so far.
tension_points.bear_case: Hyperscalers with negative free cash flow keep borrowing, AI risks spill into the broader economy in 2027, and investors who cleared supply on price alone are nearing their limit. The article says 14bps of widening could look like the bull case.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Goldman says more than price will be needed in 2027, namely clearer monetization and funding plans from hyperscalers. Absent that, supply digestion fails.
